Inter Weight Rescaling Study (df-udt @ 416)

Model: workspace/model/New416_SAEHD (df-udt, 416, e_dims=80, ae_dims=320). Input: already-aligned target.jpg. Forward: repo leras (DeepFakeArchi, opts=udt); preprocessing BGR + [0,1]. All metrics are computed inside the XSegLite mask (workspace/model/XSegLite/xseglite.onnx, 256x256 NCHW).

1. Why bicubic looks better

dense1 weights are a C x n x n field; resampling it is filtering that field. Kernel responses:

kernelresponseeffect
nearestflataliasing / blocking
bilinearsinc^2, heavy passband droop (~-4 dB near Nyquist)weights smeared, face looks soft
bicubic (Catmull-Rom, a=-0.5)flatter passband (~-1 dB)detail preserved, separable and cheap
areaboxcorrect only when downscaling; too soft when upscaling

High frequencies in the weight field carry identity detail, so the flatter the passband the closer the converted model stays. Bicubic's negative lobes only cause mild overshoot, invisible after sigmoid.

2. Interpolation is still not optimal

The quantity to preserve is the functional <W, f>. After rescaling f' ~ (L x L) f, so we need

(L x L)^T W' = W            ... (1)
  • upscale (m>n): underdetermined -> minimum-norm W' = (LxL)[(LxL)^T(LxL)]^-1 W
  • downscale (m<n): overdetermined -> least squares W' = [(LxL)(LxL)^T]^-1 (LxL) W

Interpolation computes (LxL)W and misses the inverse filter. With Tikhonov regularisation ((L^T L + lam I)^-1 up, (L L^T + lam I)^-1 down) this becomes a practical algorithm: inter_adv.py (pinv).

pinv beats bicubic for every upscale target (PSNR +0.8..1.6 dB, SSIM +0.02..0.05, cosine +0.02..0.03) at the cost of slightly higher MAE (sharper output). At 320 bicubic keeps the best PSNR while pinv lam=0.1 wins on MAE and cosine; downscaling is lossy either way.

3.1 Data-driven correction: negative result

Dual ridge regression on real activations (96 video frames, ls_correct) made things worse: 384 19.61/0.730 (cos 0.785) vs bicubic 23.32/0.813 (0.906); 448 22.36/0.809 (0.817) vs 23.41/0.834 (0.939); 512 14.02/0.755 (0.541) vs 20.26/0.814 (0.915). Reason: F' has no strict linear relation to W, so the fit absorbs image-content differences; 96 samples cannot constrain 16k-164k dimensions without heavy overfitting.

4. Recommendations

  1. Bicubic clearly beats bilinear/nearest visually - confirmed by data.
  2. pinv is better: use lam~1e-4..1e-2 for upscaling, lam~0.1 for downscaling.
  3. The data-driven LS correction is a negative result - do not use it.
  4. Every method is a warm start; fine-tune after rescaling (optimizer state is dropped).

5. Reproduce

 runtime\engine\python.exe app/tools/bench/inter_adv_study.py     # 48 masked comparisons (pinv / ls)
 runtime\engine\python.exe app/tools/bench/inter_study_run.py     # original 16 (bilinear family)
 python app/tools/bench/inter_resample.py --src <inter.pth> --res 416 --to 448 --method bicubic --out <out.pth>

Code: app/tools/bench/inter_adv.py (interp matrix L, pinv, ls_correct), xseg_mask.py (masked metrics). Data: results_adv.json (48), results.json (16), latent_metrics.json.

6. Going further: the blended solution (recommended)

pinv applies the full inverse filter, which over-sharpens weight high frequencies (higher MAE); bicubic under-shoots. On the same grid a convex combination W' = a*pinv + (1-a)*bicubic is equivalent to partial inverse filtering (Wiener shrinkage: full inversion is not optimal under noise/quantisation).

targetbicubicpinvblend a=0.5blend a=0.75

38423.32 / 0.813 / 13.3724.12 / 0.866 / 11.9723.89 / 0.846 / 12.7224.06 / 0.859 / 12.35

51220.26 / 0.814 / 18.7821.19 / 0.837 / 19.0023.80 / 0.842 / 8.8823.07 / 0.845 / 13.24

a=0.5 beats both bicubic and pinv on all three metrics at 448/512 (at 512 MAE drops from ~19 to 8.88). At 384 full pinv is still best; at 320 a=0.5-0.75 is the balanced choice.

7. A dedicated learned linear map (gradient-trained dense1)

encoder/decoder are resolution-agnostic and dense1 is linear, so W' can be optimised directly on the end-to-end output (inter_learn_study.py: pinv init + Adam + 64 video frames):

448PSNRSSIMMAE
bicubic23.410.8348.80
pinv24.980.8729.20
blend a=0.525.690.8866.58
learned (400 steps, ~5 min GPU)23.330.89014.32

The learned map has the best SSIM (0.890) but clearly worse PSNR/MAE (underfit: 400 steps, batch 8; pixel L1 also favours averaged solutions) at the highest cost. Conclusion: prefer the closed form; a learned version only pays off with thousands of steps plus perceptual losses - which is training a model, not converting one.

8. Final recommendation

448/512 (upscale): W' = 0.5*pinv(lam=1e-4) + 0.5*bicubic
384              : W' = pinv(lam=1e-1)  (or blend a=0.75, nearly identical)
320 (downscale)  : W' = blend a=0.5-0.75 (PSNR vs MAE trade-off)
avoid            : nearest; plain bicubic (512 MAE is >2x worse)

Implementation: inter_adv.resample_inter(mode='pinv', lam=...) plus the convex mix in inter_blend_study.py. All metrics computed inside the XSegLite mask.
